title: A mutex guard must be dropped before a call that waits on another thread
rule: Before calling anything that blocks on another thread (a request/reply over a channel such as Watcher::ask, a join, a recv), make sure no lock that thread may need is held. A guard made in a `match` scrutinee or an `if let`/`while let` condition lives to the end of that statement, so `match self.lock().sources() { Ok(s) => other_thread_call(&s) }` keeps the lock across the call. Bind the value in its own statement first (`let sources = self.lock().sources();`). Test it deterministically: hold the lock the other thread takes first, let it reach its wait, start the call on a third thread, release, and assert the call returns within a timeout.
rationale: E51.1 (#599): `sync_watch` matched on `self.lock().sources()` and called the watcher thread inside the match; the watcher, mid-change, held the file index and waited for the index lock, so adding or pausing a source while fonts arrived froze the app.
